brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut — they keep 8.5% profit vs 4.8% peer typical, so there's margin to share.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc on the 28 mm cap (market shows modest headroom at higher volume)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 8.5% profit vs 4.8% for similar firms — that extra 3.7 points is room in their price. Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — so our target is market-fair and achievable.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹2.15 L in cash for us

brief.financialLeverage: Triveni is healthy: they keep 8.5% of every ₹100 they sell as profit, carry zero debt (0.00x), and sit firmly in the safe zone (Altman Z 6.18). But their cash is stuck for 124 days — longer than similar firms at 114 days — so they feel the pinch when customers pay late. We're a tiny customer at 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue, which limits our solo pull. The play: bundle volume or a longer contract, name one of the big alternates (Manjushree, Mold-Tek), and tie faster payment to a price cut — saving them 15 days of tied-up cash is valuable when money cycles slowly.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B (65/100), makes pharma bottles and caps — a top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B (73/100), strong in pharma containers and closures — a robust alternate for bottles and caps.

risks: We're only 0.15% of their sales — too small to move the needle alone; bundle more volume, a multi-year lock, or threaten to shift a chunk to Manjushree or Mold-Tek.
EPF payment delays flagged in their risk profile — watch that any new agreement includes a clause on statutory compliance and penalty for lapses.
Their cash cycle is 124 days vs 114 peer median — they're slower than similar firms, so pushing payment terms too hard without sweetening price may backfire if they can't deliver on time.
Market backups listed (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads from web research — not yet qualified or priced; verify capabilities and audit before issuing any RFQ.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing our packaging price in line with the market — you're keeping 8.5% profit vs 4.8% typical, so let's find 10–15% savings and tighten payment terms to 30 days so we both free up cash.
